title: AI-written contracts - enforceability questions lawyers should prepare for
p1: A contract written by AI can look perfect, sound professional, and still create a legal headache. The surprising part? The biggest risk may not be the wording itself, but who is responsible when the machine gets something wrong.
p2: Many people assume that if an AI-generated contract is signed, it is automatically as valid as one drafted by a lawyer. That is not always the case. Questions around review, accuracy, intent, and accountability can become critical when a dispute arises.
p3: AI can help create drafts faster, but human judgment remains essential. Lawyers will need to examine whether the agreement reflects the parties' real intentions, whether important terms were missed, and whether proper review happened before signing. The future of contract work may involve AI assistance, but responsibility will still belong to people.
conclusion: If an AI creates a contract that both parties sign, who should be responsible if a major mistake is discovered later?
